messages.content: Can you put the three San Diego flights on the same footing for both of us? Include one shared checked bag, and tell me what the restrictions actually mean. We have the $3,600 cap and are going with the single beach hotel.

Yes. I’ll compare the complete round-trip cost for two travelers with one checked bag in each direction, then add the same $1,921 after-tax hotel total to each. Are the November 8-13 dates still fixed?
They are fixed. We cannot add a night on either side.

Here is the normalized comparison. All three have one stop each way and morning departures from San Diego on November 13.

Alaska: $968 for two tickets, plus $70 for the shared bag round trip, so $1,038 for air and $2,959 with the hotel. It leaves MSP at 6:05 a.m. and reaches San Diego at 11:18 a.m. The fare cannot be changed voluntarily; cancellation returns only a partial credit, not cash.

American: $1,012 for two tickets, plus $80 for the shared bag, so $1,092 for air and $3,013 with the hotel. It leaves at 8:40 a.m. and arrives at 2:05 p.m. Changes are allowed without a separate change fee, but any fare increase is due. Cancellation produces a travel credit valid for one year from ticketing; it is not refundable to the card.

United: $1,136 total, including the shared checked bag, so $3,057 with the hotel. It leaves at 11:15 a.m. and arrives at 4:42 p.m. Changes are allowed with fare difference, and cancellation returns the ticket value as a future-flight credit. No cash refund applies.
So none of these is actually refundable to the card?

Correct. These quoted fares are all nonrefundable. The practical distinction is that Alaska is the most restrictive if your plans change, while American and United preserve the ticket value as carrier credit, subject to their validity rules. A fully refundable fare would require repricing.
How much room does each leave under the total budget?

With the $1,921 hotel held constant: Alaska leaves $641, American leaves $587, and United leaves $543 under the $3,600 airfare-and-lodging ceiling. Those cushions do not include meals, local transportation, or optional seat charges.
The United one seems hard to justify. It costs more and loses most of Sunday.
Agreed for this itinerary. Its flexibility is similar to American’s, but it costs $44 more after baggage and arrives 2 hours 37 minutes later. There is no offsetting advantage in the quoted terms.
Between Alaska and American, are we basically paying $54 to avoid the harshest ticket rules?

Yes. American is $54 more in normalized airfare. That buys changeability and retention of the full ticket value as a credit if canceled, while still keeping you $587 below the fixed airfare-and-hotel cap. The tradeoff is arriving at 2:05 p.m. instead of 11:18 a.m., which gives up 2 hours 47 minutes in San Diego.
For this trip I’d rather protect that first afternoon. The dates are firm, and getting there before lunch is worth more than the extra flexibility. Select Alaska, but don’t purchase it yet.

Alaska is selected for the November 8-13 comparison, with no purchase made. The booking-stage total is $1,038 for two round trips including one shared checked bag, plus the $1,921 single-hotel total, for $2,959 combined. That is $641 under the $3,600 cap. Before purchase, recheck the exact flight times, connection duration, baggage price, partial-credit cancellation rule, seat fees, and both final after-tax totals; any change in fare or hotel price should be reconciled against the cap.
